title: Bollobás-Meir TSP Conjecture Holds Asymptotically
summary: In 1992, Bollobás and Meir showed that for every $k \geq 1$ there exists a constant $c_k$ such that, for any $n$ points in the $k$-dimensional unit cube $[0, 1]^k$, one can find a tour $x_1, \dots, x_n$ through these $n$ points with $\sum_{i = 1}^n |x_i - x_{i + 1}|^k \leq c_k$, where $x_{n + 1} = x_1$ and $|x - y|$ is the Euclidean distance between $x$ and $y$. Remarkably, this bound does not depend on $n$, the number of points. They conjectured that the optimal constant is $c_k = 2 \cdot k^{k / 2}$ and showed that it cannot be taken lower than that.
